content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Route53 healthchecks for euw2/azb showing >75% probe loss and multiple synthetic check failures in the last 5m. Alert group: /alerts/region-euw2/probe-loss. Escalate to oncall.

maria: ack, I'm on it. I'm seeing the alerts in Console. Route53 check failures correlate with missing metrics in our monitoring.

kevin: checking CloudWatch raw logs for the healthcheck targets — host-side http returns 200 from vendor pings. So probes seem to reach origin. Could be telemetry ingestion (kinesis) or our metric pipeline.

anya: I can confirm Grafana shows a sharp drop in 'probe_reports_received' for euw2-probe-cluster-3 starting ~5m ago. No errors in the probe agent itself in the last hour from the vendor UI.

opsbot: ran quick diagnostics against metric forwarder: `curl -s https://internal-metrics.euw2/api/health` -> `{"status":"ok","lag_seconds":12}`. Kafka topic offsets look healthy.

maria: interesting — vendor cw logs show probes arriving, but our monitoring ingestion counters not incrementing. Could be a processing worker been OOM killed or a temporary IAM permission issue.

kevin: I'm tailing the ingest worker logs on infra-prod-euw2-processor-2: ```
[2026-03-15T12:07:02Z] INFO  Received 102 events
[2026-03-15T12:09:10Z] WARN  Sink write retries to metrics-db: 5
[2026-03-15T12:11:34Z] ERROR Failed to write batch: timeout
[2026-03-15T12:11:34Z] ERROR Shutdown: out of memory
```

anya: OOM on processor-2 — that would explain missing telemetry. Any automatic restarts?

opsbot: systemd reports a restart at 12:12:10Z but thereafter the process repeatedly recovers then hits OOM. Memory spikes to ~95% on that host.

maria: ok mitigation plan: 1) temporarily mute the noisy Route53 alerts for euw2 (so we don't page everyone), 2) scale up processor group to add nodes and prevent OOM, 3) routefailover: enable region fallback policy for customer-facing endpoints if healthchecks remain degraded >15m, 4) notify SRE oncall for processor scaling.

kevin: agreed. I'll scale the processor ASG by +2 and restart the failing instance after investigating heap usage. Running: ```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name euw2-metrics-processor --desired-capacity 6
```

maria: I'm muting the Route53 alert group to avoid paging. Doing now.

support-bot: Posted status update to incident channel /status-page: "Investigating missing telemetry from euw2 probe ingestion. Users may see elevated synthetic failures; internal teams are mitigating."

anya: quick note — this is a monitoring-only symptom so far; upstream BGP/Route53 records are fine and customer traffic isn't impacted yet. But keep an eye on routing policies if synthetic checks stay down.

opsbot: ASG scale command returned success. New instances provisioning. Healthchecks for processors showing warm start.

kevin: new processors up. I'm pulling heap dump from the old instance for postmortem. For now, ingestion counters beginning to recover: `probe_reports_received` trending back to baseline over last 3m.

maria: good. Re-enabling the Route53 alert group will cause pages again — I suggest we keep it muted for another 10m to observe stability, then re-enable with an elevated threshold.

dakota: taking handoff in 10m. Quick summary for incoming oncall: root cause likely ingestion worker OOM on euw2-processor-2 causing missing monitoring telemetry which in turn triggered synthetic Route53 alerts (false positives). Actions taken: muted alerts, scaled ASG +2, restarted failing instance, collected heap dump, posted status update to customers. Current state: telemetry recovering, no customer-facing impact observed.

maria: thanks dakota — please also verify the heap dump and open a Jira for remediation: upgrade JVM memory limit and add OOMGuard to the service.

dakota: will do. Jira created: PROBE-8721. Assigning to infra-team.

support-bot: Customer impact note appended to external status page: "No request errors observed; synthetic monitoring anomalies being mitigated. We'll update with timeline after root cause analysis."

kevin: one follow-up: the processor had a memory leak pattern after a version push 48h ago. We should correlate deploys. Pulling deploy logs now.

maria: ok that's important for RCA. For now, I will schedule the alert group to be re-enabled at +15m with threshold: `probe_loss > 25% for 5m` (was previously 10%).

opsbot: scheduled alert re-enable at 12:30Z with new threshold.

dakota: handing off — I'll monitor for next 30m, escalate to eng-sre if telemetry dips again. If you see Route53 healthchecks go to 100% failure and origin 200s are still present, treat as monitoring pipeline issue, don't run traffic failover until we confirm origin unreachable.

maria: noted. Thanks all. Leaving logs and heap dump link in /incidents/2112233344/artifacts.

support-bot: Final note: external status page updated: "Mitigation in progress; monitoring restored. Incident remains open for postmortem and follow-up."

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigation actions applied (alerts muted, processors scaled). Monitoring recovery observed. Please add any additional findings to PROBE-8721.

dakota: closing handoff. If anything degrades I'll reopen the thread. :thumbsup:
